mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average indicates an easing monetary policy stance, which reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return in periods where FEDFUNDS is declining is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.5% and remains elevated for two consecutive months, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in less than 40% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a broad-based economic slowdown, which triggers a negative feedback loop in corporate earnings and risk appetite, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both INDPRO and HOUST decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high consumer spending (RSAFS > 750000), rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong household demand and economic momentum, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in periods when RSAFS > 750000 and HOUST is rising, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) reflects robust manufacturing activity and economic expansion, which supports corporate earnings growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when INDPRO is rising, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.5%, it signals persistent inflation that may trigger a monetary policy tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in less than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or the Rank IC for the interaction is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), a decline in the year-over-year change of CPI (CPIAUCSL) signals that inflation is cooling, which reduces the risk of an over-tightening cycle and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening cycle with cooling inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL YoY decline, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.
